utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Okay, I think everyone's here. Yuki, you made it, good.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Yeah, sorry. Train was slow.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: No worries. Before we start, did anyone see Klara's note about the shared drive cleanup?

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Saw it. Ignored it.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Marco.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: I'll do it Friday.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Um, I think maybe I already moved most of my folders? Not all of them, though.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Fine. Whatever's left, just get it done by end of week.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: Can we get to the conference thing? I've got a call with the venue people at three and I want to know where we stand.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: We'll get there. Let me do two quick things first. Rosa wants the quarterly swag order numbers by Thursday.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Which swag?

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: The stuff for the spring roadshow. Pens, the notebooks, whatever else.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Notebooks are done. Pens are late.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Late how?

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Supplier says next week. Maybe.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: I could, uh, chase them? If that helps.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Okay, Sven, you chase. Tell them we need a firm date, not a maybe.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Right, a firm date. Sure.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: The notebooks, are those the ones with the new logo?

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Yeah, the green one.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Good. The old one looked washed out.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Okay. So, the customer conference. Henrik, you've been itching.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: Yeah, so, I've been thinking about this since January. I want a proper two-day event in Prague, around 300 customers, in October.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Prague specifically.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: Prague specifically, yeah. Good flights from most of where our customers sit, and the venue is solid.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: October's crowded though.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: It is, but the hall is open the week I want.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Okay, let me push on this a little. Why does it have to be in person? Everybody's tired of travel.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: Because the numbers say so. The venue's held at thirty-eight thousand for both days, and that's a hold, not a quote.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Thirty-eight, okay.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: And last year, the people who came in person rated it seventy-one on satisfaction. The webinar crowd gave forty-four. That's not close.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: That's, um, quite a gap, I think.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: And sponsors picked up about sixty percent of the bill last time, so we're not eating all of that.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Sixty of what, though? Total?

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: Total cost, yeah. Roughly. I'd have to check the sheet for the exact split.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Devil's advocate again. Sponsors only cover that if they get booths. Are they going to want booths again?

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: Tadeusz said two of them already asked.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Tadeusz at which company?

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: The logistics one. He's on their partner side.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: I talked to Ibrahim last week, actually. He said his team would come if it's not on a holiday.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Which holiday?

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: I don't know. Something in late October, I think. I didn't look.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: There's nothing that matters in Czechia then, I checked.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Okay. I'll just tell him that.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Hold on, going back to an earlier thing. Sven, what was the swag supplier called again?

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Um, I think it's Brightline? Or Brightwell. One of those.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Brightwell.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Yeah, Brightwell, thanks.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Okay. And does anyone know if Zofia is still doing the badge printing?

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: She moved to the other floor. Oksana has it now.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Oh. When did that happen?

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Like three weeks ago.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Nobody tells me anything.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: It was in the thread.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Which thread?

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: The one with the, uh, the reorg stuff. It was in there.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Okay, I skim those.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: I think maybe everyone skims those, honestly.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Moving on. Actually, side thing, has anyone tried the new expense tool?

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: I did. It rejected my receipt twice.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: It said the image was blurry. It wasn't blurry.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: It does that.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: You have to hold the phone really still. Like, unnaturally still.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: That's ridiculous. I'll mention it to finance.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: I think maybe the, um, the desktop upload works better? I had it working on desktop.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: I'll try that.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Okay. Back to the conference, because Henrik is going to explode.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: I'm not going to explode.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: He's a little bit exploding.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: Look, the hold on the hall runs out at the end of the week. If we don't confirm, they release it.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: End of this week?

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: Friday, yeah. They sent an email.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: And the thirty-eight covers the whole venue, nothing extra?

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: Venue and the basic setup. Catering is separate, AV is separate.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: So thirty-eight is not the total.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: No, it's not the total. Nobody said it was.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Just checking.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: What do we have for catering, roughly?

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: Rough guess, another thirty, give or take. I haven't gotten real quotes.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: I think maybe we should, uh, get a couple of quotes before we, um, lock anything?

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: Quotes for catering, sure. That's separate from the hall.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Right, right. That makes sense.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Yuki, you've been quiet. Anything bothering you about it?

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Not really. I just wondered about the hotel block. Is that something we handle or the venue does?

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: The venue has a partner hotel. They hold rooms for us.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Okay, good. Then I don't have a problem.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Marco?

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Fine with it.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: That's it? Fine?

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Numbers look right. Hall's available. What else do you want?

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Nothing, I'm just surprised you're not arguing.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Save it for catering.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Okay. Henrik, you've heard everyone, and I've got nothing left to poke at. Go ahead and sign the venue contract before Friday.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: Great. I'll get legal to look at it first, then send it over.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Yes, run it past Klara's people, they're quick.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: Will do.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Do I, um, need to do anything on my side for that?

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Not yet. Just the pens.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Right. Pens. Got it.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: I can start on the invite list if that's useful.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: That'd be great, thanks. Pull from last year's attendees first.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: All right, I have to jump to another call. Thanks, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Okay, I see everybody. Henrik, you look like you've already been in three meetings.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: Two. The second one ran over.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Let's start with the boring one. Did Rosa get the pen date?

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Um, yes, I think? The supplier wrote back, it's the, uh, the fourteenth of March.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Is that firm or a maybe?

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: I think maybe firm? It's in an email, with the word "confirmed" in it.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Forward it to me.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Sure, yeah. After this.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Good. Then Rosa can stop asking me.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: She'll ask about something else.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: She will. Okay, the badges. Oksana, has she sent the proof?

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Not yet. Said Thursday.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Thursday of this week?

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Or next. She wasn't clear.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Hm. I'll ping her.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: Can I jump to the conference? I'm only here till half past.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: You always are. Go on.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: So the invites have been out since last Wednesday, and the hotel people want a rooming estimate. I told them I'd get back to them, so-

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Sven had the registration export. Sven?

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Oh. Um, yes. I pulled it this morning, I can, uh, read it out?

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: So, it's, uh, two hundred and ten in. Out of the three hundred places.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: Already? That's way faster than last year.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Right, I think so, yes. But there's, um, a couple of things in the, the comments field that I think maybe matter.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Such as.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Well, thirty-eight of the ones registered are from Asia-Pacific, and they all asked in the notes if there'd be some kind of remote access. Like a stream or something. And, um, three of our biggest accounts told the account managers they can't come. Company travel ban. It's not about the date, it's a ban.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: All thirty-eight?

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Yeah, I counted twice. It's thirty-eight.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: That's, what, under twenty percent of what's in. We can't redesign the whole-

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Which three?

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: I don't have the, um, names in front of me. I think Ibrahim's team is one of them? I'd have to check.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: Ibrahim said he'd come.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: He said that before. I think the ban came after.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: Huh. I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Is the ban for the whole year?

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: I don't know. The note just said "until further notice".

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Okay, hang on, so let me take the other side for a second. Travel bans come and go. By October it may be gone.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: Right, exactly. October is eight months away.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Might. Might not.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: I'm not saying it will. I'm asking whether we plan around something we can't see.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: I think maybe, um, that's fair, but also we can't see the other thing either?

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Meaning what?

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: That it, uh, goes away. Sorry, I don't know. I think I just mean either is a guess.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Fair. Yuki, you've gone quiet again.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Mm. I was thinking about the three accounts.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Go on.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Those are the ones we most want in the room. Sponsors care about them, sales cares about them. If the event is only in person, we're closing the door on exactly those people.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: And the Asia-Pacific people aren't a footnote either. They registered anyway. They want to be there somehow.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: Sure, but the satisfaction numbers-

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: I know the numbers. Those were people who came. It doesn't tell you about the ones who couldn't.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: That's, okay. That's a point.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Hm.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Marco, you're doing the face.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: What face.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: The "I have a number" face.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: I don't have a number. Just, a stream costs money.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: How much?

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: No idea. Haven't asked anyone.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: So we don't know it's even affordable.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Okay, so nobody here knows the cost of any alternative, and nobody knows how long the ban lasts.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: I could, um, ask the AV people? For a rough price. If that helps.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Hold that thought, I'm not sure we're at that point.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Oh. Okay. Sure.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: Honestly, I'm not thrilled about changing things now. The hall's locked in.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: I'm not saying drop the hall.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: Then what are you saying?

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Just that it can't be the end of the conversation. Three big accounts is not nothing.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: Fair. I'm not saying it's nothing.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Okay. Let me back up a second. Is the three-accounts thing confirmed, or is it hearsay through account managers?

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Um, it's through account managers, I think. I only have what they typed into the sheet.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Then somebody should talk to them directly.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Not me.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: I didn't say you.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Just clarifying.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: I can talk to Tadeusz's side, the partner folks. They hear things.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: That's not the customers, Henrik.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: No, but they hear things.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: I can check with the account managers. Which ones asked.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Okay, Yuki, you do that. Names, and whether it's a travel ban or something softer.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: Wait, I need to go in a couple minutes. Can I say one more thing?

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Quickly.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: The hotel estimate. I need to tell them something. I'll say we're at two-ten and growing, and nothing else.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: That's fine. Say that and no more.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Speaking of growing, the shared drive thing is still there. Klara's note went round again.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Ugh. Did she say a new date?

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: End of month.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Um, I think I'm done with mine. Mostly.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Mostly.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: There's one folder I can't open. Permission, I think.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Tell Klara.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Okay, yeah, I will.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm going to drop. Someone send me the notes?

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: I'll send them. Go.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: Thanks. Bye.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Okay. So where does that leave us. Yuki is checking the accounts. Anyone else have thoughts before we stop?

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Not now.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Um, I think maybe I'll send the, the export to everyone? So we're all looking at the same one.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Yes, do that. With the comments column.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Can you sort it by account size?

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: I think so, yeah. I'll try.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Good. Same time next week, then. Ibrahim's team can wait till Yuki knows more.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Okay, thanks all.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Okay, I think everyone's here. Yuki, you're on mute. Or - no, you're fine, I see the bar moving.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Sorry, my headset keeps switching to the laptop mic. Can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Loud and clear. So, before the add-on stuff, quick one on the status page migration.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Oh, is that the one Anders was doing? Because I talked to him Friday and he said it was basically-

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Elif, hold that thought, I've got the update in front of me. Anders says it's pushed to the week of the 17th.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Right, right. The 17th. That's what he told me too, I just forgot.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: Why did it slip? It was supposed to be this Friday.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Something about the DNS records needing sign-off from Laszlo's group. Two business days, supposedly.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: Two business days always means a week.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Probably. Okay, moving on. Thandi sent the support ticket numbers, and the, uh, the volume is up about 18 percent on last month.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Is that the billing tickets or everything?

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Everything. Billing is maybe a third of that. I can send the breakdown after.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Yeah, send it. I want to see if the invoice PDF thing is still-

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: The invoice PDF thing was fixed, I think. Wasn't it? Leila said she shipped it before her trip.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Not what I heard, but okay.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Let's take that offline, I'll ask Leila. Right. The add-on. Pricing. We have the launch window locked for April, so we need to land this today if we can.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: Today? We haven't even looked at the numbers properly.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: We've looked at some of them. I put the comparison in the doc last week, did anyone open it?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: I skimmed it. Kind of. I got to the part with the, um, the competitor table and then I got pulled into something else.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Okay. Fatima, you did the interviews, right? Did you have a view on it?

utterances.speaker: Fatima
utterances.text: Yeah. Um. A little one.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Go ahead, whenever you're ready.

utterances.speaker: Fatima
utterances.text: So what if we just - the flat thing. Forty-nine a workspace, per month, and no seat limit. Unlimited seats.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: Flat forty-nine. Okay. Just so I'm clear, that's the whole add-on? Nothing on top?

utterances.speaker: Fatima
utterances.text: Nothing on top, yeah.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: That's, uh, that's cheaper than I expected. Like, a lot cheaper than what we floated in January.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: January was per seat, if I'm remembering right. Eight dollars, maybe nine.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Eight-fifty.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Eight-fifty, thank you. I have it in the sheet somewhere.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: So why flat? Per seat is the normal thing. Customers get used to it, finance can forecast it. Flat looks like we're leaving money on the table.

utterances.speaker: Fatima
utterances.text: Well. I mean. When I was talking to the admins, it kept coming up.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: What kept coming up?

utterances.speaker: Fatima
utterances.text: Nine out of the twelve said that if it's per seat they'd just - they'd hold back on who they invite. Keep it to a few people.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Oh that's interesting, that's the opposite of what we want for a collaboration tool.

utterances.speaker: Fatima
utterances.text: And the, um, typical workspace has about fourteen people in it. The median I mean. So at forty-nine that's roughly three-fifty each.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Three-fifty is about right, forty-nine over fourteen. A bit over, actually, three-fifty-ish.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: Okay, but the median hides the big ones. The workspaces with two hundred people are paying the same forty-nine as a team of five.

utterances.speaker: Fatima
utterances.text: Yeah. That's true.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: And those are the ones who'd pay more. I'm just saying, we're giving away the top end.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Although the top end is, like, tiny. How many workspaces are over a hundred?

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: I'd have to pull it. I want to say under thirty out of something like nineteen hundred.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: See, so it's-

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: Under thirty that matter a lot, though. Those are the logos.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: The logos aren't paying us extra now either-

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Okay, okay, one at a time. Zainab, fair point, I'll pull the real number so we're not guessing.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Can I ask something kind of sideways? Does the add-on need the new permissions model? Because if it does then the large accounts are going to have a whole other conversation with sales.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: It uses the existing roles and groups, no new model. Sorry, existing permissions. I misspoke.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Oh good. That's what I was hoping.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: Does anyone know what the competitors do? The table had, um, three of them?

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Two are per seat. Eleven and fourteen dollars. One is flat but it's tiered by workspace size, so it's sort of a hybrid.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: So we'd be the only pure flat one.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Among those three, yes.

utterances.text: Hm. That's either a selling point or a red flag.

utterances.text: That's accurate. Keep going, you're doing fine.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Um, cost. He had it at about twenty-eight a head. So for all of us, 220 people, it comes to, what was it, 6,160. Something like that.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: 6,160, yeah. I got the quote from the supplier on Wednesday, it's good until the end of next month.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: And there was a test run. Fifteen people had them for, I don't remember, a few weeks? And nobody opened a ticket. Not one.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Three weeks. Fifteen people, zero tickets. I checked Caio's queue to be sure.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Zero is a nice number to see after what we saw last week.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Was the pilot, um, was it people who like this stuff? I think maybe that skews it?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Fair question. It was mixed. Two from finance, three from the warehouse office, the rest were us and the helpdesk.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Okay. That's, yeah, that's more mixed than I assumed.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Can I put the text message numbers next to that? For the cost side?

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Gateway was coming out around two cents a message, like Wei guessed. Over a year that's a few hundred, not a lot. So the codes are cheaper, no question.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Cheaper but we had one get through in the first month.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: I'm not arguing. Just saying the difference is about six thousand, give or take.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: And six thousand is less than one executive mailbox incident would cost us, if somebody ever looked at it that way.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: I wouldn't put a figure on that.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: No, me neither.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Okay, devil's advocate time, and Mateo, I know it's usually you, but I'll do it. What about the people who lose them?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Lose the keys? Yeah, that happens. You order a few spares. The quote has twenty extra in it, I think. Or ten. I'd have to look.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Twenty. Page two.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Page two, there you go.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: And if someone's on holiday and loses it?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Then they call the helpdesk and we send a spare. It's not elegant. Neither is waiting for a carrier to answer.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Fair.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: What about the warehouse people? The ones without phones on the floor?

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: That was the twelve. A key doesn't need a phone, so that actually clears that one.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Oh. Right. I think maybe I forgot that part of the list.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: It was in the note, bottom of the first page.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: I keep getting distracted. Sorry. My sister called me at lunch, she's finally unpacked and wants to host everyone, and I said yes without thinking about who'd be doing the cooking.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Fourth floor, still?

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Fourth floor, still. We are all going to be carrying wine up the stairs.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Bring a spare key, in case she forgets hers.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Ha. No. Okay. Stop. Back.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: How long to switch everyone over, if it came to that? We have the end of April.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Delivery's about ten days. Then it's handing them out. I'd say small group sessions, twenty people at a time, so we're not doing 220 one by one.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Eleven or twelve sessions then.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Roughly. Could be ten if people come in bigger groups.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Do they all need to be in person?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Better if so. Ten minutes each, you register it, you test it, you leave.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Could I help with a session? I think maybe I'd be okay at that.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Yes please. I'd like two people per session anyway.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: And the old text codes stay on during all that?

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: They'd have to. Until the last session at least.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Right, that makes sense. So nobody locked out halfway through.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: And managers first again, I'd say. Like last time.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Sure. One day ahead, same as before.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Mailbox note goes to Samir as well, I'd guess.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Cc Samir, yes, he likes to know. And Clara needs a line before the end of next week, I'm not going to make her find out from the audit tracker.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: I can write that one. Short.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Thank you. Keep it dry. No adjectives.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: I don't do adjectives.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: You do, a few. Okay.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Mateo, I'm happy with all of this. Can you place the order today, and get the group sessions on everybody's calendar before the end of next week? Wei will help you run them.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Yep, I'll send the purchase request after this and book the first slots for the week after next.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Do you want me to forward the quote to finance, or will you?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: I'll do it. I have the PDF open.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Okay. Their sign-off is usually a day or two.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Tell them it's tied to the audit date, that tends to speed them up.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Will do.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: I can start on the instructions for the sessions. I think maybe a one-page thing?

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: One page. With pictures if you can.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Okay, I'll try.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Should I mention the spares in the note to Clara?

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Just the count, no detail. She'll ask if she wants more.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: The laptop quotes, by the way. Finance finally replied. They want it as one line in next quarter's request.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Of course they do. Fine, I'll write it up Monday.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: I'll send you the vendor names again.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Please. Okay, I've got a call at the top of the hour, so I have to run.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Same here, honestly.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Thanks, everyone. Good week, actually, despite everything.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Bye.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Okay, um, can everyone hear me? Diego, you're unmuted, good.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Yeah. Learned my lesson.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Who's got notes? I did them last time, so-

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: I'll do them. Well, I'll try. I'm bad at typing and listening at the same time.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Thanks. So, uh, before the patch window business, I want to pull the contractor laptops back up. Last week it was the seven weeks and the price sitting there, and I don't love that we just left it hanging.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: Good, because I've been holding something since Friday.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Hang on. Are we actually reconsidering, or are we just talking ourselves back into the same answer?

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: I mean, looking at it again. That's all. Chloe, you had the money side, right?

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Yeah, so, forty-three seven or thereabouts for the buy, then seven weeks where nothing's different, and half those people rotate out by autumn. That's what bugs me.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: Can I- sorry. Diego, did the vendor put the lead time in writing?

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Yeah, it came through the portal. Seven weeks. They said they'd ship a first batch sooner if we split it, but, um, not by much.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: So the gap is real.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: It's the gap, and also owning machines for people on six-month stints. I just can't make that sit right.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: Okay, that's what I wanted to get to. The vendor also does a rental thing, it's about thirty-eight dollars a unit a month, six-month terms. Which is basically how long most of these engagements run.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: And for the gap, we switch off prod access from anything unmanaged starting in week two. Alejandra's agency and the data one both wrote back that they're fine with that.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Thirty-eight a month. So, what, fourteen hundred a month for the lot?

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: Closer to fourteen-fifty. Call it nine thousand for the six months, if nobody extends.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Against forty-three seven. Okay, that's a different conversation.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Unless they extend. Then you're renting forever.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: Sure, but when someone leaves it goes back in the box. No wiping, no reissuing, no chasing the return form.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Still managed by us though? Same image?

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: Same trimmed image, our profile. The vendor just owns the hardware.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Okay. Then imaging's the same job.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Why week two? Why not week one?

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: Week one they're getting set up, you have to let them in somewhere. Week two the block goes on.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: And the agencies are really okay with that? Last week they were threatening to pull people.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: That was about carrying a second laptop. This is the reverse, they carry ours and nothing else.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Which two was that again? Alejandra's and the data one?

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: Yes. Diego has the emails.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Yeah, both replied Monday. I'll forward them again.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: What about the twelve with no disk encryption? They'd be covered once the block is on?

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: Anyone reaching prod would be on a managed disk, so yes. That's what I'd send the auditor.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Not before week two, though.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: No. After the block's actually in.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Fine. I'm running out of objections, which is annoying.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Diego, anything from you?

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Um. Just, the rentals have a return date, right? Somebody has to track it.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: It's renewable at six months. I'll add a column to the order sheet.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Does finance mind that it's monthly instead of one purchase?

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: I'd have to ask them. Hardware line, other line, I never remember which is which.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: I'm fairly sure rental is the operating side. That's honestly easier.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Good. Okay, so, the company-managed laptops for the contractors in prod, all thirty-eight, that's where we are. Zainab, you keep the order moving.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: Yep, I'll update the draft today.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Do I get to stop now?

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: You never stop.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Ha. True.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Patch window. Still Sunday night?

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: Sunday night is fine, I'm on call anyway.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Me too, evening's okay. I've got a thing in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: I'm out until Monday noon, so, not me.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Right, Zainab and Kwame. Chloe, the VPN gateway cert, where's that?

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Waiting on Milan. I pinged him twice.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: It expires on the thirtieth.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: I know, I know. I'll go stand at his desk.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: He's remote.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Then I'll stand at his screen.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: I can message him too if you want.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Yes please, double pressure.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Okay. Sione's lunch, did anyone sort a time?

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: Thursday, noon, I think.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Is Tomasz coming?

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: He said maybe. He says maybe to everything.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Tomasz said something about the onboarding batch too. Does anyone remember the date?

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: First week of April, last I heard.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: That's this week. Okay. Okay, noted.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Are the notes going to the usual list?

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Yes, please. And add the vendor emails.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Will do. Zainab, which page of the audit do you want attached?

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: Page four. Or five. I'll just send you the whole thing.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Great, that's what I expected.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Anything else? I have a call at the top of the hour.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Nope, I think that's it. Thanks, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Okay, I think we're all here. Tariq, you can hear us?

utterances.speaker: Tariq
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm on.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Good. So, the in-office thing. Leadership wants one policy for every team, and apparently it's us writing it up.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Anika's note said she wants a draft before the all-hands.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Right, which is the end of the month. Before that, did the survey numbers come back?

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Mostly. We got 214 responses, so about seventy percent of the company, give or take.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: That's actually decent for an internal survey.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: It is. The free text is a mess though, I'm still tagging it.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: I skimmed a chunk of it. Some people want total flexibility, and a couple basically want everyone back five days.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Five days isn't happening.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: No, no, I'm just saying the range is wide.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: So what are we actually choosing between? I only see a blank page right now.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Fair. Nothing formal yet. Tariq, you said something in the channel last week, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: Tariq
utterances.text: Yeah, um, a little. Two set days for everybody, Tuesday and Wednesday, the same across all teams. That's what I'd put forward.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Okay, so a hard anchor, not a "pick your own two."

utterances.speaker: Tariq
utterances.text: Right, not pick your own.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Why those two, though? Why not Monday and Thursday, or whatever people happen to like?

utterances.speaker: Tariq
utterances.text: Well, so, the desk booking numbers. Those two days are already the busiest. Sixty-two percent of attendance lands there.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Sixty-two of the total, or of the people who book at all?

utterances.speaker: Tariq
utterances.text: Of bookings, I think. Total badge swipes would be a bit lower, I'd have to check.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Okay, I can pull the swipe data after this.

utterances.speaker: Tariq
utterances.text: And the last group of new joiners, they said they felt pretty isolated. Half of them were barely overlapping with anyone.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Yeah, I remember that. Bao told me one of them went three weeks without seeing their own team lead in person.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: That's not great.

utterances.speaker: Tariq
utterances.text: And, uh, if the days are fixed, meetings across teams actually land. Right now you can't get finance and us in one room.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Sure, but fixed days means everyone commutes the same days. Trains are packed, desks are packed.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Desk capacity is a real thing. If sixty-two percent is already the peak, are we sure there's room for a hundred percent?

utterances.speaker: Tariq
utterances.text: Not a hundred. Remote folks and part-timers wouldn't all be in.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Facilities said the floor holds about eighty percent of headcount, I think. I'll confirm with Marta.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Eighty of what, the current headcount or the plan for next quarter?

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Current. I'll ask.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: I just want to be sure we're not picking the first thing someone said.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Sure, but it's the only thing on the table. If you've got another one, put it out there.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: I don't, honestly. I'm poking at it.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Can I ask something slightly off topic?

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Go ahead, quickly.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Zofia's leaving do, is it Friday or next Friday? I never got the invite.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Next Friday. Petra's sending the thing around today.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Okay, cool. I'll get a card going.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Put me down for a few pounds on that.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Done.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Back to this. Lena, what did the survey say about days people already prefer?

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Hang on. Um, let me find it. Okay, among people who answered on days, Tuesday and Wednesday came up the most, then Thursday.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Thursday's close?

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Not that close. Maybe ten points behind, it's in the sheet.

utterances.speaker: Tariq
utterances.text: That fits the booking data anyway.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: And the Friday thing, nobody wants Fridays?

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Hardly anyone. People like their long weekends.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Honestly the only complaint I heard was childcare on Wednesdays for a couple of people.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Hm. How many is a couple?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Two, three? I'd have to ask.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Okay, that's something we handle with an exception process, not by moving the days.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Who approves the exceptions?

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: The line manager, with us just keeping the log.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Fine by me.

utterances.speaker: Tariq
utterances.text: Yeah, that sounds workable.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: There's also the question of what happens in weeks with a public holiday.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Let's not get into the holiday weeks right now, that's a footnote.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Okay, I'll note it.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: One more devil's advocate thing. If it's all teams, is sales going to be fine with this? They're out at clients half the time.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Client days count as working, they won't be penalised. Yara in sales ops said the same last week.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Okay. Then I don't have a real objection.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Me neither. It's simple, which helps. People remember two days.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Simple for the comms, too. One line on the intranet.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Right. So, I don't think we need to go around again. Everyone is in the office on Tuesdays and Wednesdays, with exceptions through the line manager.

utterances.speaker: Tariq
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: I'll write that into the draft tonight.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Good. And Lena, the swipe data when you can.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Yep, tomorrow morning at the latest.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Do we want to tell people before the all-hands, or wait?

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Wait for Anika. We take the draft to her first.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Makes sense.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Can I send her the survey summary in the meantime?

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Lena, is the summary fit to send?

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Not yet, the free text isn't finished. Maybe Monday.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Monday's fine.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Also, did anyone sort out the laptop refresh schedule? I got a ticket that says mine's due.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: That's IT, not us. Just reply to the ticket.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Alright, will do.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Okay, I've got another call in two minutes. Thanks, all.

utterances.speaker: Tariq
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Okay, are we all on? Tariq, I can see you, good. Right, before the policy stuff, did Anika reply about the draft timing?

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: She did, she's fine with Thursday next week for the first read.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Good, that's -

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Sorry, quick one, did the card for Zofia go round? I put in my bit on Monday.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Petra has it, ask her. Anyway, Lena, the swipe data, did you get that?

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Yes, sent it yesterday afternoon. Tuesday and Wednesday are the peak, same as the bookings, a bit lower overall.

utterances.speaker: Tariq
utterances.text: Okay, so it holds up.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Roughly, yeah. Fifty-eight, fifty-nine percent on the two days, from memory.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Fine. And Marta said the floor does take about eighty percent of current headcount, so capacity isn't the problem.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Eighty, so we're okay on the two days as long as remote folks stay out.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Right. Which brings me to - Mateo, you said you had something?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Yeah, so I was in a catch-up with Yara's team, not about this, and they mentioned the pulse survey, the short one that went out last month.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: The quarterly one?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Yes, that one. And I looked at the commute question, because I was curious.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Which cut did you use?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: People with a commute over ninety minutes. About a third of them, thirty-four percent, said they'd think about leaving if the days get fixed.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Thirty-four of how many? That group's small, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Not tiny. Maybe sixty people? I'd have to look. And, um, two of the engineering resignations in the last few weeks, both exit notes mention the policy talk.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Wait, both of them?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Both. One says it outright, the other is more, you know, hints.

utterances.speaker: Tariq
utterances.text: Hm.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Okay. That's not nothing.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: No, it's not. If a third of the long-commute people are thinking about walking, then fixed days is a problem. Replacing an engineer runs us far more than whatever we gain from people overlapping on Tuesdays.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Hold on, though, devil's advocate. Thinking about leaving in a survey isn't leaving.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Sure, but two already did.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Two, and one of them was barely about the policy.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: The second one was fairly clear -

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Let's not relitigate the exit notes. Tariq, you proposed the days. Anything?

utterances.speaker: Tariq
utterances.text: Um. I mean, the isolation thing for new joiners is still real. That didn't go away.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: I'm not saying it did.

utterances.speaker: Tariq
utterances.text: I just - it's why I raised it.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Right. Okay, so where are we. The days stay as the draft says until we have a better picture. Lena, can you get the actual numbers on the long-commute group?

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: I can ask for the raw cut. Probably Monday.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Monday is fine. Don't tell Anika yet, I'll mention it when I see her.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Can I ask something separate? The new joiner point. Tariq, you said some of them go weeks without seeing anyone.

utterances.speaker: Tariq
utterances.text: Yeah. Three weeks for one of them.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Because that's a thing we could look at on its own, right? Without touching the days.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Meaning what?

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: What if every new hire gets a buddy from outside their own team? Someone to just ask things.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Oh, like Bao did for me, kind of.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Bao was on your team though.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Yeah, true, he was.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Is there a reason it needs to be outside the team?

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Eight of the last eleven new hires told us they didn't know who to ask outside their own team. Eight out of eleven, I counted from the onboarding forms.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Okay, that's pretty convincing.

utterances.speaker: Tariq
utterances.text: Yeah. Whoever's on their team, they already have.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Who picks the buddy?

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: We could do it, from a list of volunteers. Nothing heavy.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: I'd volunteer. I know half of finance.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: You know half of finance because you talk to them for an hour at a time.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: That's networking.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: How long does the buddy commitment last?

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: First three months? Weekly check-in, fifteen minutes, something like that.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Three months seems long. Six weeks maybe.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: We can argue about that, it's a detail.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Fine. Okay, cross-team onboarding buddies, approved. Chloe, draft the one-pager and we'll fix the length when it's written up.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Sure. I'll send it by Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Good. Mateo, you're the first volunteer, apparently.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Happy to.

utterances.speaker: Tariq
utterances.text: Do we need to tell the managers?

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Yes, I'll mention it in the leads meeting on Friday.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Which Friday? The one after Easter?

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Oh, right, it's the holiday weekend. Then the Tuesday after.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Speaking of the holiday, is the office actually open on Monday? My badge email said something odd.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: It's closed Friday and Monday. The email was just wrong about Monday.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Okay, good. I'd rather not find out at the door.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Back to the policy for a second. If the commute numbers hold, what would we even do about it?

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: I don't know yet. That's what the raw cut is for.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: There are a few things people could look at. Half days, a later start on anchor days, something like that.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Hold that thought, Lena. Let's see the data first.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Tariq
utterances.text: Can I ask, do the engineers know their exit notes are being talked about?

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: No, and let's keep it that way. This stays in this room.

utterances.speaker: Tariq
utterances.text: Right, sure.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Should I forward you the survey cut, Lena, or do you want to pull it fresh?

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Forward it, then I'll check what they used for the commute buckets.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Will do after this.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: And the safe assumption is the days stand in the meantime, yeah?

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: For the draft, yes. We haven't changed anything.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Anything else? I've got to jump in a minute.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Nope.

utterances.speaker: Tariq
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Just the card for Zofia, I'll chase Petra.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Good. Thanks, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Okay, is everyone here? Tariq, I can see you, good.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Anika moved the first read to Thursday afternoon, by the way.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Yeah, I saw. Before that, did the survey cut come back?

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Last night. The proper long-commute numbers are in the shared sheet.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Oh nice, so I wasn't completely making it up.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: We'll see. Okay, since the results are in, let's sit down and go through the days again, properly. I'd rather look at it now than after the all-hands.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Good, because I had a feeling that thirty-four percent was going to haunt us.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: It's real, it's just the denominator that I want to talk about.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Go on.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: So the long-commute group, over ninety minutes each way, is eighteen people. Out of three hundred and ten staff on the roster.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Eighteen? I said sixty, didn't I.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: You said maybe sixty, and you said you'd have to look.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Yeah, okay. I was way off. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: It's fine. That's why we asked for the cut.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Still, eighteen people is eighteen people. If a third of them go -

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: A third of eighteen is six, give or take.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Six engineers is still a lot of money.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Replacing one costs us months of recruiting, I'd say, plus the ramp-up.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Months, yeah. Took Bao's team nearly five to fill the last one.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Sure, but let's not jump. Tariq, you proposed the days. You've been quiet, what do you make of it?

utterances.speaker: Tariq
utterances.text: Um. So, yeah. Six people, that's what the thirty-four percent actually is. Six out of three hundred and ten.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Six who said they'd think about leaving, not six who'd be gone.

utterances.speaker: Tariq
utterances.text: Right. And, uh, we already have the exception thing. If someone's commute is really long, their manager can approve it. That's been there since the first meeting.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Has anyone actually used it, though?

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Four requests so far, I have the log. All four approved.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Four, okay.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Four of eighteen is a decent share, then.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: About a quarter, yeah.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: Tariq
utterances.text: And the two resignations. I read the exit interviews again. One of them took a promotion at another company. The other one moved cities.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Wait, but the one note said something about the policy.

utterances.speaker: Tariq
utterances.text: It mentioned the talk, yeah, in passing. But the reason given was the move.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Huh. I read that as a harder complaint, honestly.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: I reread it too. The relocation is what it's about, the policy line is one sentence at the end.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: So neither of them left over the days.

utterances.speaker: Tariq
utterances.text: That's how I read it.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Okay, devil's advocate again. Maybe they just didn't want to say.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: They were exit interviews with Bao, they said plenty of other stuff. They weren't shy.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Fair.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Sorry, so what I told you two weeks ago -

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: You flagged what you saw, that's what we want. It just turned out smaller.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: To be fair to the pulse survey, the question was hypothetical. People answer "would you consider leaving" very generously.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: That's true. I always say yes to that kind of question and I'm perfectly happy here.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Same, I'd say yes just to sound spicy.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Wonderful. Okay, moving on - Tariq, the isolation thing, is that still the main reason for you?

utterances.speaker: Tariq
utterances.text: Mostly, yeah. And the cross-team meetings. If everyone's in on the same days it's much easier to get finance in a room.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Facilities numbers back that up, don't they? Marta said eighty percent capacity.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Right, and the two days run at about sixty percent of bookings now, so there's space.

utterances.speaker: Tariq
utterances.text: And the new joiners, the ones from March, two of them told me they finally met their lead on a Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: That's a fair point for fixed days.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: I felt that when I started. Nobody was ever in on the same day.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Was that before the buddy thing?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Before, yeah. The buddies start next month, right, Chloe?

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: First pairs go out in May. The one-pager's done, I just need Mei's sign-off.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: I'll look at it tonight, remind me.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Sixty-two, from the bookings. Fifty-eight or nine on swipes.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Whichever. It fits.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Should I add a line to the draft about the long-commute exception? Make it more visible?

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Yes. Put it near the top, so nobody has to hunt for it.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Okay, I'll say managers can approve it for commutes over ninety minutes, and we keep the log.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Can I ask a different thing? What about people who live far and are on the train?

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: That's the commute number, that's the same group.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Right. I mean the ones just under ninety.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Hm, there'd be a cluster around eighty, I'd guess. I can check the sheet.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Even a handful would be good to know.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: A handful, I'd say. I'd rather look than say.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Don't build a new category off a guess. The manager can use judgment on the edge cases.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Fine. I'm not pushing.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Unrelated, are we doing the team lunch thing Thursday? I need to know for the catering form.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Thursday we're meeting Anika at two, so lunch before that, quickly.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Twelve-thirty then. I'll put in for ten.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Make it eleven, Petra said she might join.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Eleven. Got it.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Is Petra bringing the cake or is that a different week?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Different week, I think. This one's just sandwiches.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Okay. Back to this. Does anyone still want to argue the days?

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: I mean, the six people thing took the wind out of it for me.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Same. Honestly I came in thinking we'd need to change something.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: I'm okay with it. Probably.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Probably?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: No, I'm okay. I just like saying probably.

utterances.speaker: Tariq
utterances.text: I'm fine with it.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Chloe, you've gone quiet.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: I'm done arguing. Not much left to argue with.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Good. Lena?

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Yeah, fine.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Good. So, Tuesdays and Wednesdays stay as the anchor days for everyone, with the exception route for long commutes. That's what goes to Anika on Thursday.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: I'll update the draft this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Do I tell my contacts in finance, or is it still quiet?

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Still quiet until Anika's seen it.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Okay, quiet.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Does Anika get the commute breakdown too?

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Send her the summary, with the eighteen and the four approved exceptions. Short.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Did anyone ever sort out Zofia's card? Petra said she'd got it.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Petra has it, it went round on Monday. You signed it, I watched you.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Did I? Okay, then I did.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Everyone signed it. It's a very full card.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Oh, one thing. Yara asked if sales can have the client-day wording in the draft as it was written.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Yes, keep it exactly as it was.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Good.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Also my laptop refresh ticket got answered. Tuesday next week.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Which is an anchor day, so you'll be in anyway.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: I'll be in, laptop in hand. Hopefully a good one.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Bring the old one for the swap.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Yeah, will do.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Okay, I have to jump to a call. Anything else quickly?

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Not from me.

utterances.speaker: Tariq
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: I'm good.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Thanks, everybody.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Okay, I think everyone's here. Noor, you're on? I can hear typing but no voice.

utterances.speaker: Noor
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm here. Sorry, was muting something.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: No worries. So, um, the annual plan stuff. We keep circling it and never land anywhere.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Right. Three weeks now.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Which, yeah. Big picture, we want more people paying for the year up front, cash is cash.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Cash is cash until they churn in month two and want a refund.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Sure, sure, we'll get to that. Yuki, you had some thoughts from the weekend?

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Um, yeah, a few. I think maybe, if it's okay, I'll start with what I'd put on the table.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: So, uh, what if we just offered fifteen percent off for anyone who prepays for the full year? Like a flat thing, nothing tiered.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Flat fifteen. Okay.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Why fifteen and not ten? Or twenty? Feels like you picked it off a shelf.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: No, no, I mean, I think there's a reason. Hang on, let me find the sheet.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: While she's looking, did anyone see the email from Davor about the offsite?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Saw it. Didn't read it.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: It's mostly logistics. Dates are the second week of September, I think.

utterances.speaker: Noor
utterances.text: I thought it was the third week.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Could be. I'll check it.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Okay, got it. So the pilot we ran, the one with the trial accounts, we had about three hundred of them.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: The pilot from March?

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: April, I think. Anyway, at fifteen percent, thirty-one percent of those three hundred ended up on annual.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: And, um, the cohort before that, with the old eight percent offer, only got to eighteen percent. So that's quite a jump.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: That's a big gap.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Sure, but was it the same kind of account? Trial users in April could be a different crowd than whoever saw the old offer.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: I mean, they came from the same signup flow. I think maybe the mix was close.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Maybe close isn't great.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Fair. I can't prove it was identical.

utterances.speaker: Noor
utterances.text: The old one ran during the holiday stretch, right?

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Mostly, yes. Some of it.

utterances.speaker: Noor
utterances.text: That might have pulled it down a bit, people are slow then.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Or pushed it up, people have budget to burn in December.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Either way the new number's higher.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Right, that's, yeah, that's kind of the point I keep making. Direction matters more than the decimals.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Direction matters, but if we give away fifteen off and it only shifts people who would've paid annually anyway, we've just cut our revenue.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Um, that's possible. I don't think the data says that though.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: The data's three hundred accounts.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Good enough for a first read.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: For a first read, sure.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Can we, uh, hold that thought a sec. Camille pinged me about the support queue.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: What about it?

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: She says the billing tickets doubled last week, and she thinks it's the invoice template change.

utterances.speaker: Noor
utterances.text: I saw some of those. People confused about the tax line.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Right. Noor, could you look at it with her? Not urgent, just, you know, this week.

utterances.speaker: Noor
utterances.text: Yeah, I can do that. I'll message her after this.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Great. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Back to the discount. What happens to monthly customers? Do they feel punished?

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: I think maybe a little, but monthly always costs more. That's kind of what it is.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: They can switch.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Some will switch and then we lose the monthly premium.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Yeah, which is sort of the goal, isn't it? Fewer people churning every month.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Fewer people churning is the goal. Lower revenue per head isn't.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Okay, but net, net, annual is stickier. We've seen that on the older plan.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: We've seen it, I'm not disputing it.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Then what are we arguing.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: I'm checking it's not fluff.

utterances.speaker: Noor
utterances.text: Can I ask something?

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: Noor
utterances.text: When someone prepays and then wants out in month four, what do we do? Because that changes how generous we can be.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Um, right now it's prorated, I believe. Klara would know better.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Klara's out till Thursday.

utterances.speaker: Noor
utterances.text: Okay. I just didn't want that to be a surprise later.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: No, good flag. We'll sort the refund bit separately.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Fine by me. But that's a real cost.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Everything's a cost.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Not every cost has a number on it.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: This one does. Prorated.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Okay okay. Let's not-

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: I'm just saying-

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: I know. I know. It's useful.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Can I add, I did also check the competitor pages. Most of them sit between ten and twenty on annual.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Which ones?

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: The three we usually look at. I can send the links.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Please. Not that I don't believe you.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: No, no, that's fair.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Middle of the range then.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Roughly, yeah.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Right. So we're not out on a limb.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Nobody said we were.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Just thinking out loud.

utterances.speaker: Noor
utterances.text: Is the pilot still running for anyone?

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: A few accounts got grandfathered. I think maybe forty or so.

utterances.speaker: Noor
utterances.text: Okay. Those would just roll over.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Presumably. I haven't checked how the billing system handles it.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: It'll be fine.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: It'll be fine until it isn't.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Then we fix it.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Let me ask a different thing. Farah mentioned the sales deck still has the old numbers on it.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Which deck?

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: The one for the mid-market stuff. I'd guess it's from the spring.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: I can ping her.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: That'd help, thanks. Mateo, just ask her what version she's using.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Will do.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: I still think we're being a little quick, but I don't have a better number.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: I mean, if you find a better one, I'd honestly want to see it.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: I'll poke at the cohorts tonight. If something's off I'll say.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Fair enough. Okay, I think that's enough for me. Sana, get the pricing page updated, would you? Maybe by the end of the week.

utterances.text: Hang on, though. Chidi does this all the time. He lays a membrane, the glue's fine, we're covered.

utterances.text: If we add the membrane, yes. That's the fourteen.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: So it's fifty-two with it. Sorry, I'm doing it in my head. Fifty-ish.

utterances.text: Don't.

utterances.text: Wait, we looked at that?

utterances.text: I think maybe I have the number somewhere. Let me look.
